title: Заселение с комфортом  (Checking In with Comfort)

segments.t: Max brings his grandparents into a plush room at Hotel Eleon. Worried about the cost, his grandmother offers to sleep on the floor at Max and Vika's apartment, so Max quickly insists they stay at the hotel in comfort and introduces them to Mikhail Dzhekovich.
Бабуль, перестань! Ну какой на полу?
А по-русски как хорошо разговаривает, да?
Now let's go back through their conversation line by line and unpack the Russian phrasing.
'Wow! Just like in the movies!' The meaning hinges on 'oh' working together with 'cinema' in spoken Russian.
'Maxim, it is probably very expensive here.' Notice how Russian expresses 'proper name' and 'probably' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
'Let us spend the night at your place.' The meaning hinges on 'let's' working together with 'will spend the night' in spoken Russian.
Бабуль, перестань! Ну какой на полу?
'Granny, stop it! What do you mean on the floor?' In Russian, the idea of 'granny' flows naturally into 'floor' without extra filler words.
'Spend the night here in comfort.' Max anchors the line on 'spend the night', while 'comfort' completes the thought.
'Hello, Mikhail Dzhekovich.' The grammar packs 'hello' and 'proper name' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'Good afternoon.' The meaning hinges on 'good' working together with 'day' in spoken Russian.
'Lyuba. Good afternoon!' In Russian, the idea of 'Lyuba' flows naturally into 'day' without extra filler words.
А по-русски как хорошо разговаривает, да?
'And how well he speaks Russian, right?' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'and' before landing on 'yes'.
'Let us go to the room.' Notice how Russian expresses 'let's go' and 'number' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
'Have a pleasant stay!' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'pleasant' before landing on 'rest'. the guest answers right away.
'Thank you very much.' the guest brings out the contrast between 'thank you' and 'very much' in a few short words. Alright, let's hear the entire conversation one more time from start to finish.
Бабуль, перестань! Ну какой на полу?
А по-русски как хорошо разговаривает, да?
And that finishes the hallway check-in scene. Listen for the verb meaning to spend the night and how Max persuades his grandmother to stay in comfort at the hotel. Until next time!
